stem: A teacher models the numbers of girls and boys who arrive late for her class on any day by the independent random variables $G \sim \text{Po}(0.10)$ and $B \sim \text{Po}(0.15)$ respectively.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the probability that during a randomly chosen 2-day period no girls arrive late.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability that during a randomly chosen 5-day period the total number of students who arrive late is less than 3.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
It is given that the values of $\text{P}(G = r)$ and $\text{P}(B = r)$ for $r \geqslant 3$ are very small and can be ignored.

Find the probability that on a randomly chosen day more girls arrive late than boys.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Following a timetable change the teacher claims that on average more students arrive late than before the change. During a randomly chosen 5-day period a total of 4 students are late.
parts.text: Test the teacher’s claim at the 5% significance level.
